name: QuietIsland
tagline: Turns the notch into a small island for what is happening on your Mac.
description: QuietIsland sits around the notch and shows what you need without a window: now playing, a Pomodoro timer, the volume and brightness display, a clipboard history, a shelf for files, and your Claude Code sessions with their approvals.
privacy: QuietIsland has no accounts and no telemetry. Clipboard history and files stay on this Mac. Its optional local API only listens on this machine and needs a token. The only internet request it can make is the update check, and that only runs if you allow it.

name: Quietbar
tagline: Controls Sony headphones from the menu bar, without the phone app.
description: Quietbar talks directly to your headphones over Bluetooth: noise cancelling and ambient sound, equalizer, multipoint, touch panel settings, battery in the menu bar, global shortcuts, and automatic profiles by app or Wi-Fi network. Tested on the WH-1000XM5. Other models are listed in the repository. Independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony.
requirements: Headphones already paired with the Mac
privacy: Quietbar has no accounts, and your settings stay on this Mac. Everything between the app and your headphones goes over Bluetooth. The only internet request the app makes is the Sparkle update check, once a day, which you can turn off. If you use a Wi-Fi profile, macOS asks for Location so the app can read the network name, and it is used for nothing else.

screenshots.alt: Quietbar panel in light mode, with sound mode, equalizer and battery

demo.heading: Automation
demo.text: When a call starts, Quietbar switches to noise cancelling on its own. When the call ends, your previous mode comes back. It works with any calling app, because Quietbar only checks whether the microphone is in use. It never listens to the audio.
demo.alt: The Quietbar panel changes from Ambient to Noise cancelling when a call starts, and back when the call ends

name: DungeonDrafter
tagline: Draws battle maps for tabletop RPGs, in 2D and 3D.
description: DungeonDrafter is a native map editor for game masters. Draw a floor plan, switch to an orbiting 3D view of the same scene, browse your own asset library, and export the finished map to FoundryVTT.
privacy: DungeonDrafter has no accounts and no telemetry, and it makes no internet requests. Your maps and assets stay on this Mac.
